newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Stanbic sees declining real S.African rates.
newsitem.headline: Stanbic sees declining real S.African rates.

text.p: South African real interest rates should decline this year, paving the way for more rapid real GDP growth in 1998 after a pedestrian two percent rise in 1997, Standard Bank Investment Corp chairman Conrad Strauss said on Wednesday.

"Inflation is expected to stay below 10 percent and real interest rates to recede from the record levels of recent times, as liquidity improves and inflation gradually falls," he said in his chairman's report.

"These developments, taken with the beginnings of a privatisation programme and with infrastructural expenditure undertaken in conjunction with the private sector, should establish a sound base for more rapid growth in 1998."

Strauss said some critical economic variables had started to move in the right direction with an improving balance of payments, continued conservative monetary policy and an expected disciplined budget in March likely to boost foreign exchange reserves.

The better economic picture should enable to banking group to record another year of satisfactory performance, Strauss added. For the 1996 financial year Stanbic reported a 27 percent rise in net taxed income to 1.552 billion rand, despite pressure on interest margins.
